title: People and family
cando: say who people are, and talk about your family

about.text: In this lesson you talk about people. You say: This is my sister. You show a family photo.
goals: Say my, your, his and her.

chapters.title: Who is that?
chapters.text:
Samir is at a work party.
His family is there too.
His friend Lena asks: Who is that?
Samir says: That's my son. He's six.
Listen for he and she.
Listen for this and that too.

chapters.title: He and she, this and that
chapters.text:
A man or a boy: he.
A woman or a girl: she.
This is near you. That is far away.
Before a person: my, your, his, her.
My sister. His wife. Her son.

chapters.title: My family
chapters.text:
Next, you read a text: My family.
Then you fill in a family form.
Write names and numbers.

chapters.title: A family photo
chapters.text:
Then you show a family photo.
Say who everyone is.
This is my mother.
Then say one more thing.
Her name is Rosa.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a family story.
Who is in the family?
Read it two times.

warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people have them on their phone.

conversation.title: Who is that?
conversation.setting: It is a work party. Samir's family is there. Lena works with Samir.
lines: Hi, Lena. This is my wife, Leila.
Hello, Leila! And who is that?
That's my son, Adam. He's six.
Her name is Nadia. She's nine.

questions.why: Samir says: This is my wife, Leila.
Samir says: That's my brother, Karim.

phrases.use: Asking about a person near you.
Asking about a person far away.
A man or a boy: he.

items.meaning: Your mother, father, brothers, sisters and children.
items.example: I call my family every Sunday.

items.meaning: A woman with a child. You say: Mum.
A man with a child. You say: Dad.
items.example: My father is in the photo.

items.meaning: A man or a boy. Your mum is his mum too.
items.example: My brother works in a hotel.

items.meaning: A woman or a girl. Your mum is her mum too.
The woman you are married to.
The man you are married to.
A boy or a man. He is your child.
A girl or a woman. She is your child.

items.example: Their new baby is a girl.

items.meaning: A person you know and like.
items.example: Omar is my friend from work.

sound.title: th in this and that
sound.explain: Put your tongue between your teeth. Push out a little air. It is not d, and not z. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Samir's lines. Record yourself. Then listen. Is your th clear?
lines: Hi, Lena. This is my wife, Leila.
That's my son, Adam. He's six.
Her name is Nadia. She's nine.

spot.instructions: Look at these lines from the conversation. They are about people.
examples: That's my son, Adam. He's six.
Her name is Nadia. She's nine.
spot.question: He or she for Adam? He or she for Nadia? Leila: this. Adam: that. Why?
spot.answer: Adam is a boy: he. Nadia is a girl: she and her. Leila is next to Samir: this. Adam is far away: that.

rules.title: he and she · this and that · my, his, her
rule: A man or a boy: he. A woman or a girl: she.
Near you: this. Far away: that.
This is my sister. That's my brother.
I → my · you → your · he → his · she → her
His name is Adam. Her name is Nadia.
rules.mistake: Not: Samir and her wife. Say: Samir and his wife.

practice.q: This is my brother. ___ is thirty.
practice.why: A brother is a man: he.

practice.q: This is my mother. ___ is a nurse.
practice.why: A mother is a woman: she.

practice.q: Your friend is next to you. You say: ___ is my friend.
The man is far away. Who is ___ man?
Karim has a wife. She is ___ wife.
practice.why: Karim is a man, so his.

practice.q: Leila has a son. He is ___ son.
practice.why: Leila is a woman, so her.

practice.q: What is ___ name? My name is Lena.
practice.why: You ask about the other person: your.

practice.q: This is my ___ . She is two.
practice.why: She is for a girl: daughter.

practice.q: Nadia is a girl. ___ name is Nadia.

practice.why: Friend: a person you know and like.

yourTurn.prompt: Think of three people in your family. Say who they are. Use he or she.
yourTurn.model: This is my husband. His name is Luis. He is forty. This is my daughter. Her name is Sofia. She is ten.

text.title: My family
text.body:
My name is Priya.
This is a photo of my family.
I am in the photo too.
The man is my husband, Raj. He is a driver.
The boy is my son, Arjun. He is eleven.
The girl is my daughter, Maya. She is seven.
The woman with me is my mother, Asha.
My father is not in the photo. He is in India.

gist.why: Priya says: This is a photo of my family.

gist.q: Who is not in the photo?
gist.why: Priya says: My father is not in the photo.

detail.why: The man is my husband, Raj.
The girl is my daughter, Maya. She is seven.
The woman with me is my mother, Asha.

detail.q: How many people are in the photo?
detail.why: Raj, Arjun, Maya, Asha and Priya: five.

items.meaning: A young person. We say: he.
A young person. We say: she.

items.example: This is a photo of my family.

model.title: Priya's family details
model.body:
FAMILY DETAILS

Your name: Priya Shah
Husband or wife: Raj Shah
Children: Arjun (11), Maya (7)
How many children? 2
Other people in your home: my mother, Asha
How many people in your home? 5

write.task: Fill in the form about your family. Copy the words from the model. Use your own names and numbers. No husband, wife or children? Write: no. It can be real or made up.
checklist: My name is on the form.
Every name starts with a capital letter.
The last line has a number.

card.title: My family photo
card.situation: Amina is your new colleague. She asks about your family. You have a photo on your phone.
card.goal: Show the photo. Say who everyone is. Say one thing about each person.

prepare.notes: Choose a photo. Write the names of three people. Write he or she for each name. It can be a made-up family.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, show a photo. Or draw your family. Say who everyone is. Your classmates ask: Who is that?
doIt.wehel: You are my new colleague. I show you a family photo. Ask me about four people. Ask: Who is this? Who is that? What's her name? How old is he? Use very simple English.

model.title: A family photo
lines: Yes. Look. This is my mother.
Her name is Rosa. She's fifty.
That's my daughter, Sofia. She's ten.
That's my brother, Pablo. He's a cook.
compare: I say who each person is.
I say a name or an age.

canDo: I can say: This is my sister.
I can use he and she.
I can ask: Who is that?
I can talk about my family.
I can fill in a family form.

reading.before: Look at the first picture. Who are the people? Is it a family?
reading.talk: Who is in the story? Write two sentences, like: This is Ana. She is thirty. Then say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: My sister is thirty. ___ is a nurse.
quiz.why: A sister is a woman: she.

quiz.q: This is my brother. ___ name is Adam.
quiz.why: A brother is a man, so his.

quiz.q: The woman is far away. ___ is my mother.
A girl or a woman. She is your child. She is your ___ .
Leila is Samir's wife. Samir is Leila's ___ .
Your husband is next to you. You say: ___ is my husband.
A very young child is a ___ .
quiz.why: A baby is a very young child.
What is your name? asks for a name.

quiz.q: How ___ is the tea? Two pounds.

liveClass: Day 1: learners show a photo on their phone, or draw their family. In pairs, they ask: Who is this? Who is that? Then practise the party conversation.
Day 2: the task. Each learner shows a family photo and says who everyone is. Classmates ask one question each.
Day 3: talk about the book. Then a he-or-she game: say a family word, and learners say he or she.
